newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Hormel Foods upgraded.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Hormel Foods upgraded.

text.p: -- Piper Jaffray analyst George Dahlman said Friday he upgraded Hormel Foods Corp to a strong buy from a buy rating, using a target price of $32 a share over the next 12 months.
-- On Thursday, Hormel reported fiscal first quarter earnings of $0.27 a share, even with a year ago, which Dahlman said was "a bit better" than his expectation.

-- "We believe (Hormel) shares are quite attractive relative to the S&P Food group; the emphasis on brand management (hence, away from commodity products), is not only continuing, but accelerating," Dahlman wrote in a report.

-- He added Hormel's expanding international activities should fuel earnings growth and raw material costs -- principally corn, soybean meal and hogs -- are expected to be more favorable over the next couple of years.

-- "Hormel's emphasis on value-added (branded) products appears to be accelerating," Dahlman wrote. "While this has been a long standing theme for Hormel, we estimate commodity fresh pork still represent(s) 25 percent to 30 percent of sales and a significantly lower portion of earnings."
-- He added that conversations with Hormel management indicate there is a growing emphasis on "reducing this exposure" from fresh pork.
